question.text: Strategic asset allocation differs from tactical asset allocation in that:

answer.text: Strategic allocation changes daily based on market conditions
Strategic allocation is based on long-term objectives and risk profile, while tactical allocation involves short-term deviations to capture market opportunities
Tactical allocation is always more conservative than strategic allocation
Strategic allocation only includes equity while tactical includes all asset classes

explanation.text: The Logic: Series X-A defines strategic asset allocation (SAA) as the long-term target policy allocation grounded in investor goals, objectives, and risk profile, while tactical asset allocation (TAA) is a short-term decision within the SAA framework to exploit market opportunities. The Trap: SAA is the stable, long-term base — it does not change daily. TAA can be either more aggressive or more conservative than SAA depending on the market view, and both spans cover the same asset classes. Note: Specific tactical tolerance bands (such as +/-5-10% from strategic weights) are illustrative and were not found in the checked X-A pages; the source-backed point is the SAA/TAA distinction itself.
